record.paper_title: Monetary Stabilization in Cryptocurrencies—Design Approaches and Open Questions
record.context_brief: Monetary targeting with short-term exchange-rate smoothing
record.original_question: Can a cryptocurrency stabilize purchasing power more sustainably by using monetary targeting, possibly combined with managed floating or short-term exchange-rate smoothing, instead of committing to a fixed exchange-rate target such as a 1-to-1 USD peg?

evidence.quote:
Monetary targeting in a sense is already implemented by
traditional cryptocurrencies with predetermined block reward.
More sophisticated monetary targeting approaches might use
literature around rule based monetary policy (e.g. [61], [62],
[63] or [64]) as ﬁrst starting point. If additional measures
against exchange rates are to be taken, managed ﬂoating
regimes as promoted by [65], [66], might offer a simple
but sustainable alternative to exchange rate targeting. This
approach, however, mitigates only short term ﬂuctuations.

While monetary targeting in
combination with short term exchange rate smoothing could
be an interesting alternative, it has largely been ignored by
cryptocurrencies.

Zooming out, we suggest that short
term smoothing of exchange rates might offer a sustainable
alternative to exchange rate targeting—the current focus of
over 90 % of projects.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a cryptocurrency system whose protocol controls the money supply through programmable issuance and possibly through interventions in secondary markets. Define the purchasing power of one unit of the cryptocurrency at time t as 1/P(t), where P(t) is the price level of a reference consumption basket denominated in units of the cryptocurrency. Consider three classes of monetary policy regimes that the protocol may commit to:

(R1) Fixed exchange-rate targeting: the protocol commits to maintaining a one-to-one (or otherwise fixed) exchange rate E(t) = E* between the cryptocurrency and a reference fiat currency (e.g., USD), by issuing or absorbing supply against reserves.

(R2) Monetary targeting: the protocol commits to a rule-based path for the money supply M(t) (for example, a constant growth rule, a Taylor-type rule, or a nominal-income targeting rule) without targeting any exchange rate.

(R3) Monetary targeting combined with managed floating / short-term exchange-rate smoothing: the protocol follows a rule for M(t) as in (R2) but additionally intervenes to dampen high-frequency fluctuations of E(t), without committing to any long-run exchange-rate level.

Let Var_T[1/P(t)] denote the long-run (T → ∞) variance of purchasing power induced by a regime, and let Pr[collapse] denote the probability that the regime fails (e.g., reserves are exhausted or the peg is broken) under stochastic demand and supply shocks.

Problem. Formulate a model in which the demand for the cryptocurrency, the reference fiat price level, and the basket prices follow stochastic processes, and determine whether there exists a rule-based monetary-targeting regime of type (R3) — monetary targeting together with short-term smoothing of E(t) — that achieves both

(a) strictly lower long-run variance of purchasing power Var_T[1/P(t)] than every feasible regime of type (R1), and
(b) strictly lower probability of regime collapse Pr[collapse] than every feasible regime of type (R1),

or else prove that no such regime exists. In particular, identify sufficient conditions on the shock processes and on the protocol's reserve constraints under which (R3) dominates (R1) in the sense above, and compare (R3) with the pure monetary-targeting regime (R2).
artifact.status_search_result: No published mathematical resolution of this design question was located. The literature on stablecoin and cryptocurrency monetary policy continues to focus overwhelmingly on exchange-rate-pegged designs, and a rigorous comparison establishing that monetary targeting with short-term exchange-rate smoothing dominates fixed pegs in cryptocurrency settings has not been demonstrated. The question therefore appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Monetary Stabilization in Cryptocurrencies
status_evidence.snippet: Suggests monetary targeting with short-term exchange-rate smoothing as a largely unexplored alternative to exchange-rate targeting in cryptocurrencies.
status_evidence.claim: The proposal is presented as an open design alternative that has been largely ignored by cryptocurrency projects.
